identity.name: Sukhothai Kingdom
native_names: อาณาจักรสุโขทัย (Anachak Sukhothai)

land.text: Sukhothai, which Si Inthrathit's side took out of Khmer vassalage ('the campaign that captured Sukhothai from Khmer vassalage', Ramkhamhaeng page)

predecessors.note: The page gives the Khmer link without a year; the founding is 1238 (infobox), about 1243 for Wyatt.

successors.note: The Sukhothai page dates the end of independence to 1438 under Ramesuan's garrison (personal union 1438-1569); its infobox says 'Annexed to Ayutthaya: 1584', which the body contradicts.

The Ramkhamhaeng page says the extent is 'speculated' (Lampang, Phrae, Nan; Phitsanulok, Vientiane; the Nakhon Si Thammarat kingdom; the Mon kingdoms; the Bay of Bengal), that 'kingdoms such as Sukhothai lacked distinct borders' and that the claims 'were intended to assert Siamese dominance'. Cliopatria adds 398 cells in 1294: Tenasserim (126 cells in Myanmar, 117 taken from Pagan's 1293 shape), the peninsula (Nakhon Si Thammarat and south), and Lao and Vietnamese uplands. The land is the 703 cells of Cliopatria's 1241 outline (916 cells) that lie outside the core: 421 in Thailand, 262 in Laos, 14 in Vietnam, 3 in Myanmar. Counterpart 'nobody': the page names no state it was taken from (the khmer-empire dossier gives the whole 1241 outline to Sukhothai in 1238). region.text: Martaban, the Mon kingdom of Wareru (Mon and Kayin), whose king 'Sukhothai acknowledged ... as a vassal king'

ledger.note: By 1287: Ram Khamhaeng recognises Wareru of Martaban as a vassal. Wareru page: 'By 1287, a diplomatic mission led by his minister Laik-Gi had successfully secured Ram Khamhaeng's support' and 'The king of Sukhothai acknowledged Gadu as a vassal king' (the sentence has no year; 1287 is the mission's 'by' date). 'Still in 1293, Wareru received assurance from Sukhothai of its continued support.' From c. 1296 Wareru ruled 'three Mon-speaking provinces of Bassein, Pegu and Martaban', which is the vassal land the 1319 end event names. Sukhothai page: 'Martaban is traditionally counted a Sukhothai tributary'. Review fix: was 1294 (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1) with the three-province shape, which includes Pegu, held by Tarabya until c. 1296. The end is 1319 (Sukhothai page); the Hanthawaddy page's 'formally independent of Sukhothai in 1330' is a conflict kept in notes.

region.text: Tambralinga (Nakhon Si Thammarat) and the peninsula to the south

ledger.note: The southern peninsula joins Ram Khamhaeng's greatest extent. 'South: subjugated "Suvarnabhumi" (likely Suphan Buri) and "Tambralinga" (Nakhon Si Thammarat)' (no date; reign 1279-1298). Page silent on the year: 1294 is Cliopatria's. Cliopatria's Malay Peninsula cells begin at Nakhon Si Thammarat. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the Ram Khamhaeng inscription page names none of these places and gives no date, so 1294 stays a bridge.

region.text: the Tenasserim coast, west of the Thai range

ledger.note: Tenasserim joins the greatest extent. The Ramkhamhaeng page 'speculates' a reach west to 'the Mon kingdoms of present-day Myanmar'; the Sukhothai page claims suzerainty 'from Vientiane to Pegu'. Page silent on the year and the region: 1294 is Cliopatria's, whose shape takes 117 cells from Pagan's 1293 shape (the Pagan dossier ends in 1297). Re-checked 2026-10-19: the Ram Khamhaeng inscription page names none of these places and gives no date, so 1294 stays a bridge.

Phrae and Muang Sua pay tribute to Ram Khamhaeng. 'North: placed Phrae and Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) "under tribute"'. Page silent on the year within the 1279-1298 reign; 1294 is Cliopatria's shape year. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the Ram Khamhaeng inscription page names none of these places and gives no date, so 1294 stays a bridge.

region.text: the northern uplands that Cliopatria's 1294 outline adds beyond the 1241 outline, Tenasserim and the peninsula (137 cells: 53 in Laos, 51 in Vietnam, 14 in Myanmar, 12 in Thailand, 3 in China)

The page claims 'suzerainty from Luang Prabang to Nakhon Si Thammarat and from Vientiane to Pegu' (no date, within the reign 1279-1298) but names no place in these 137 cells; 1294 is Cliopatria's year. Added in the review pass so that every cell of the 1294 enlargement has an event; 107 of the 137 cells lie inside Cliopatria's Lan Xang of 1363 and leave with the northern dominions in 1299.

1298: Ram Khamhaeng dies and the northern tributaries break away. 'bonds of vassalage ... fell apart soon after his death in 1298'; 'The dominions north of Uttaradit ... broke free', including Muang Sua and Vieng Chan (undated). The Yuan History gives 1298; Cœdès thinks Loe Thai took over 'shortly before 1318'.

region.text: the dominions north of Uttaradit, 'among them the Lao kingdoms of Muang Sua and Vieng Chan Vieng Kham', read as the 406 cells of the 1362 shape that lie inside Cliopatria's Lan Xang of 1363 (the Lao uplands)

ledger.note: c. 1299: the northern dominions break away. Sukhothai page: 'The tributaries fell away quickly after his death' (Ram Khamhaeng, 1298); 'The dominions north of Uttaradit, among them the Lao kingdoms of Muang Sua and Vieng Chan Vieng Kham ... broke free'. Lan Xang page: after Ram Khamhaeng's death 'both Vieng Chan Vieng Kham and Muang Sua were independent Lao-Tai mandalas until the founding of Lan Xang in 1353'. Loe Thai page (summary): Uttaradit split off first and the Laotian states followed soon after, without years. 1299 reads 'soon after his death in 1298'. Review fix: replaces the 1363 loss to lan-xang (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1): the Lan Xang page does not say Lan Xang took land from Sukhothai ('victorious in defense of their territory' in the 1360s), and its gains (Vientiane in 1357) belong in the lan-xang ledger. Counterpart is the breakaway Lao mueang (no dossier).

region.text: Nakhon Si Thammarat and the peninsula to the south, the 165 cells of the 1294 shape that lie in the Southern Thailand region

ledger.note: c. 1300: the peninsula leaves. Sukhothai page: 'To the south, Suphannaphum Kingdom and Nakhon Si Thammarat left early in Loe Thai's reign'. Loe Thai reigned 1298-1323 (Loe Thai page, lead and infobox), so 'early' is a window of the first years and 1300 is my bridge inside it. Review fix: replaces the 1375 loss to ayutthaya-kingdom (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1), a transfer the page does not state; its 1349 invasion and 1378 submission made Sukhothai 'a tributary' and 'a vassal' only.

region.text: the Chao Phraya plain south of the core (387 cells of the 1363 shape: Phitsanulok, Phetchabun, Kamphaeng Phet, Nakhon Sawan, Phichit, Uthai Thani, Chai Nat, Suphan Buri, Lop Buri)

ledger.note: c. 1300: Suphannaphum leaves. Sukhothai page: 'Suphannaphum Kingdom ... left early in Loe Thai's reign'; Loe Thai page: Suphan Buri 'also broke free early in the reign of Loe Thai' (summary; the page names Suphan Buri, not Suphannaphum). The page names only Suphannaphum; the region is the rest of the 1363 outline beyond the core, Tenasserim and the peninsula (cell reading), so it also holds Phitsanulok and Kamphaeng Phet, which the page ties to Sukhothai: a limit of Cliopatria's north-western core, kept. Replaces the 1375 loss to ayutthaya-kingdom.

region.text: Martaban and the Mon provinces of Wareru

ledger.note: 1319: Martaban breaks away. 'In 1319, Martaban in the west broke away.' The Hanthawaddy page has 'formally independent of Sukhothai in 1330' (conflict kept in notes).

region.text: the Tenasserim coast west of the Thai range, the 129 cells of the 1294 shape in Myanmar

ledger.note: 1319: Tenasserim leaves with Martaban. 'In 1319, Martaban in the west broke away.' The page does not name Tenasserim; it is Cliopatria's 1294 addition on the western edge of the claimed realm, tied to Martaban's breakaway (review fix, a bridge). Counterpart 'nobody': the Wareru page says Wareru 'did not control other former Pagan territories farther south such as Tavoy (Dawei), Mergui (Myeik) and Tenasserim (Taninthayi)', and no page names its holder; Cliopatria's Ayutthaya of 1375 covers it.

1363: Lithai moves the capital of Sukhothai to Phitsanulok. 'In 1363, Lithai moves the capital of Sukhothai kingdom to Phitsanulok'; the page ties the move to Ayutthaya 'invading neighboring provinces to the south'. The Sukhothai infobox gives Song Khwae from 1347.

region.text: the core of Sukhothai (Sukhothai, Si Satchanalai, Phitsanulok), 'the Northern Cities'

ledger.note: 1438: Ayutthaya takes Sukhothai in a personal union. 'Ramesuan presumably brought Ayutthayan officials and a garrison with him, which ended Sukhothai's independence'; the page dates the union 1438-1569. The word 'presumably' makes the mechanism, not the year, uncertain; Cliopatria moves the core to Ayutthaya in 1450.

1438: Sukhothai ends as an independent kingdom. Page conflict: body 1438 ('ended Sukhothai's independence'), infobox 'Annexed to Ayutthaya: 1584'; the northern cities 'remained royal' and Sukhothai rebelled briefly in 1462 with Lan Na (the Ayutthaya page: Phitsanulok became the principal capital 1463-c.1488).

wars.name: Ayutthaya's invasion of Sukhothai of 1349
wars.outcome: Ayutthayan armies 'invaded and made Sukhothai a tributary'.
wars.note: The page's date; Ayutthaya's conventional founding is 4 March 1351 (Ayutthaya page). The tribute is a suzerain's event, carried by the Ayutthaya dossier; no ground is shown to change hands.

wars.name: Lan Xang-Sukhothai war of the 1360s
wars.outcome: 'Fa Ngum again led Lan Xang to war in the 1360s against Sukhothai', in which Lan Xang 'was victorious in defense of their territory'; no land changes hands on the page.
wars.note: The decade is the page's; the page gives no battles. 'from' and 'to' span the decade. Review fix: the Lao uplands were not lost to Lan Xang in 1363; the Sukhothai page has them break free after 1298 (ledger 1299), and the Lan Xang page says they were 'independent Lao-Tai mandalas until the founding of Lan Xang in 1353'.

wars.name: Ayutthayan subjugation of Sukhothai (1378 and 1438)
wars.outcome: 'In 1378 Lue Thai submitted as a vassal'; in 1438 an Ayutthayan garrison 'ended Sukhothai's independence'.
wars.note: The page also has Intharacha of Ayutthaya installing Ban Mueang as Borommapan (in its succession account) and Sukhothai rebelling briefly with Lan Na in 1462 (after the end).

certainty.note: A mandala of city-states: the page says 'kingdoms such as Sukhothai lacked distinct borders'; no frontier of this state is fixed by treaty or survey.

notes:
Page budget (5) spent, plus three pages for the review fixes (Loe Thai, Wareru, Ram Khamhaeng inscription) and re-reads of Sukhothai Kingdom and Lan Xang on 2026-10-19. No page gives an area, so the area check was not possible.
Review fixes (se-01-d review): the 395,000 km2 outline of Cliopatria (1294-1362) is kept only for 1294-1298. The page names what left: the dominions north of Uttaradit (Muang Sua, Vieng Chan) after 1298 (ledger c. 1299), Suphannaphum and Nakhon Si Thammarat 'early in Loe Thai's reign' (c. 1300), Martaban in 1319 (with Tenasserim, a bridge); the kingdom was 'soon back to what it had been, a small local power', drawn as Cliopatria's 1375 core (63,192 km2) from 1319. The 1241 outline (271,851 km2, 4.3 times the core) is used only for 1279-1293; 1238-1278 is the core. The 1363 loss to lan-xang and the 1375 loss to ayutthaya-kingdom were removed (the Lan Xang page: Lan Xang 'victorious in defense of their territory', no cession; Ayutthaya's 1349 and 1378 acts made Sukhothai a tributary and a vassal, no land). The vassal_start over hanthawaddy-kingdom moved to 1287 (Wareru page).
Disagreements and limits: (1) the reviewer orders the southern losses after 1319; the pages put them 'early in Loe Thai's reign' (1298-1323), so they are at c. 1300, before Martaban's 1319. (2) The exact years 1299 and 1300 are my readings of 'soon after 1298' and 'early in the reign' (confidence 2); the 1279 gain and the 1319 Tenasserim loss are bridges (confidence 1). (3) The Loe Thai page (summary) says Uttaradit itself split off first and that 'Phrae Tak' became free in 1321; the Sukhothai page says the dominions north of Uttaradit, and after 1321 only that Lan Na gained influence over Tak. Cliopatria's core holds Uttaradit (24 of 25 cells), Phrae (25 of 25) and Tak (41 of 58), so I kept the Sukhothai page and did not carve them out. (4) Cliopatria's core lies north-west of the page's Northern Cities (17 of Sukhothai province's 21 cells, 5 of Phitsanulok's 37; the city cells of Sukhothai and Phitsanulok are outside), so the 1300 loss of the Chao Phraya plain also takes Phitsanulok and Kamphaeng Phet and the capital dot of 1363-1438 lies outside the drawn shape; no page draws a better core, so it is kept. (5) Counterparts 'Muang Sua and Vieng Chan', 'Tambralinga' and 'Suphannaphum Kingdom' have no dossier. (6) khmer-empire's 1238 loss names the whole 1241 outline; only the core (213 cells) is Sukhothai's in 1238, and the other 703 cells are Sukhothai's 1279 gain from 'nobody'.
Page conflicts: Martaban breaks away 1319 (Sukhothai, Loe Thai) against 'formally independent of Sukhothai in 1330' (Hanthawaddy page); Sukhothai infobox end 1584 against body 1438; capital Song Khwae from 1347 (infobox) against Lithai's 1363 move; Lithai's death 1368 against 'the end of his reign in 1369'; Loe Thai's reign 1298 (Loe Thai page, Yuan History) against Coedes' 'shortly before 1318' (Sukhothai page).
Gazetteer cell checks (not pages): Ayutthaya's 1450 gain (213 cells) is 212 cells of Sukhothai's 1449 shape; the 406 northern cells lie inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape; the 681 cells beyond the core in 1363 are 129 in Myanmar (Tenasserim), 165 in the Southern Thailand region and 387 on the Chao Phraya plain, and lie inside Ayutthaya's 1375 shape.
Suzerainty is carried by the suzerain: ayutthaya-kingdom needs vassal_start 1349 (tributary) and vassal 1378-1438 over this state and a gain in 1438; lan-xang the gains of 1353-1357 (Vientiane) from the breakaway Lao mueang, not from Sukhothai; hanthawaddy-kingdom the end of the tribute in 1319; pagan-kingdom the loss of Tenasserim. No rulers strip: the page's list is incomplete after 1399 and its early dates disagree.
